articles.title: Google Is Quietly Gutting Its Cybersecurity Teams. Sundar Pichai's AI Bet Eats Its Own.
articles.excerpt: Mandiant analysts — the $5.4 billion acquisition that was supposed to be Google Cloud's crown jewel — are among the latest casualties of AI restructuring.
articles.image_caption: Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai
articles.nri_angle: Google employs tens of thousands of Indian engineers, with Hyderabad and Bengaluru hosting some of its largest offices. Cloud has been a major H-1B sponsorship pipeline, and restructuring there directly affects Indian-origin engineers in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Is Now America's Top Reason for Firing People. Indian Tech Workers Are in the Crosshairs.
articles.excerpt: Challenger data shows 87,714 AI-linked job cuts in five months — already more than 2024 and 2025 combined. The H-1B math is getting grim.
articles.image_caption: The Googleplex in Mountain View — emblematic of a tech industry now using AI to justify sweeping workforce reductions (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals hold ~73% of H-1B visas, predominantly in tech. With 60-day grace periods and 116,000+ tech cuts in 2026, the layoff-to-deportation pipeline is an existential concern for NRI workers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Made Anthropic's Cybersecurity A-List. Only a Handful of Firms Got In.
articles.excerpt: Project Glasswing's expansion gives Indian government agencies and IT firms access to Claude Mythos — the AI model that found 10,000 critical vulnerabilities in its first weeks.
articles.image_caption: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at TechCrunch Disrupt 2023
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT firms like TCS and Infosys could build Mythos-powered cybersecurity offerings for global clients. NRI security professionals at Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, and Microsoft now work alongside AI that can outperform human analysts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Sovereign AI Defense Startup Just Raised $30 Million. It Powers the Country's Counter-Terrorism Nerve Centre.
articles.excerpt: Innefu Labs builds the AI that India's intelligence agencies use daily — and it just secured funding to go global and prepare for an IPO.
articles.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh — India's sovereign AI defence ecosystem, which Innefu Labs powers, operates under the ministry's strategic umbrella (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: For Indian Americans in cybersecurity and defense tech — and NRI investors watching India's emerging defense-industrial complex — Innefu Labs represents a rare bet: an indigenous AI company that already has ₹100 crore in government contracts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Supreme Court Just Drew the Line on AI in Courtrooms
articles.excerpt: Draft regulations ban algorithmic sentencing, risk scoring for bail, and AI-only judicial decisions — while explicitly encouraging courts to adopt the technology for everything else.
articles.image_caption: The Supreme Court of India complex in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American lawyers, legal tech professionals, and NRI investors in judicial AI companies need to understand India's sweeping new framework — it will shape the largest common-law AI governance experiment in the world.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zepto Is Filing Its IPO Papers This Week. India's Quick-Commerce War Goes Public.
articles.excerpt: The 10-minute grocery delivery startup is targeting a ₹11,000 crore listing by July — one of the largest Indian tech IPOs of 2026.
articles.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India, where Zepto aims to list in what could be one of the largest tech IPOs in Indian market history (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors tracking India's consumer tech boom have a new decision to make: Zepto's July IPO will test whether quick commerce can generate public-market returns, not just venture capital enthusiasm.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX Is About to Become History's Biggest IPO. Indian Investors Should Read the Fine Print.
articles.excerpt: Elon Musk's $1.77 trillion rocket company lists June 12. It lost $4.9 billion last year and gives shareholders almost no voting power.
articles.image_caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 first stage lands at Landing Zone 1 after a mission
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin SpaceX engineers face complex tax implications from pre-IPO grants going liquid; NRI investors evaluating the IPO must contend with Musk's 82% voting control and a company that burns billions annually; the deal marks the start of a new asset class — pre-profit AI infrastructure companies — that will reshape NRI tech portfolios.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tim Cook's Last Keynote. Apple's Billion-Dollar Bet on Google's AI.
articles.excerpt: WWDC 2026 on Monday will unveil a Siri rebuilt on a custom Google Gemini model, running on NVIDIA Blackwell chips. It is Tim Cook's final act as CEO — and his most consequential.
articles.image_caption: Tim Cook, Apple's outgoing CEO, at a March 2026 event
articles.nri_angle: Apple employs tens of thousands of Indian engineers in Cupertino, Austin, and Hyderabad; the Ternus-Srouji leadership team values hardware — which is what Indian chip design teams build; Google's Gemini team has significant Indian-origin talent; the new Siri Extensions API opens a distribution channel to 1.5 billion devices for Indian app developers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Chip Designers Just Landed on a Global Stage. France Is Watching.
articles.excerpt: Three semiconductor startups — building analogue chips, gallium nitride defence components, and edge AI processors — will represent India at Bharat Innovates 2026 in Nice.
articles.image_caption: A 12-inch silicon wafer — the foundation of modern chip design. Three Indian semiconductor startups will showcase at Bharat Innovates 2026 in France (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Over 100,000 Indian semiconductor professionals work in the US at NVIDIA, Intel, Qualcomm, and Broadcom; India's chip design ecosystem is shifting from a services play to building indigenous products; the $19 billion India Semiconductor Mission creates return-to-India career and investment opportunities for NRI engineers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Blackstone-Backed AirTrunk Just Pledged $30 Billion to Build India's AI Backbone. The Race for Compute Is On.
articles.excerpt: Australia's largest data centre operator plans 5 gigawatts of capacity across India, joining a stampede of hyperscaler investment that now exceeds $250 billion in commitments.
articles.image_caption: A hyperscale data center facility — AirTrunk has pledged $30 billion to build AI infrastructure across India (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors and professionals tracking India's data infrastructure boom — the country is becoming a global AI compute hub with massive implications for tech careers, return-to-India decisions, and cross-border investment opportunities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nikesh Arora's Palo Alto Networks Hit $3 Billion in Revenue. He Just Declared the 'SaaS-Pocalypse' Dead.
articles.excerpt: The Indian-origin CEO's cybersecurity empire crossed $200 billion in market value as AI-driven threats prove that more intelligence means more work for defenders, not less.
articles.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks, at TechCrunch Disrupt
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin CEO Nikesh Arora leading one of the most valuable cybersecurity companies in the world — career signal for NRI professionals considering cybersecurity, and investment thesis for diaspora investors watching the AI security trade.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Intel Just Made Its First Major Bet on India's Chip Ecosystem. The $3.3 Billion Facility Will Make What Goes Under the Processor.
articles.excerpt: A glass-core substrate manufacturing plant in Odisha, backed by Intel's process expertise, marks the chipmaker's first significant participation in India's semiconductor mission.
articles.image_caption: Intel headquarters in Santa Clara, California — the chipmaker has announced a $3.3 billion advanced packaging facility in India (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI semiconductor engineers and investors tracking India's push into the chip supply chain — Intel's Odisha move creates career pathways for returning professionals and opens a new investment corridor in India's industrial east.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Tech Workers Powered Dallas's Housing Boom. Now They're Leaving, and Prices Are Cratering.
articles.excerpt: The H-1B crackdown, 123,000 tech layoffs, and a $100,000 visa fee have turned North Texas suburbs from the hottest real estate market in America into a cautionary tale for Indian homebuyers.
articles.image_caption: A for-sale sign stands in front of a suburban home
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian H-1B workers and their families bought homes in Frisco, Prosper, and Celina. They are now the population most directly affected by the housing correction — facing underwater mortgages, 60-day visa clocks after layoffs, and the question of whether to sell at a loss or wait it out.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI Data Centres Are Hoarding the World's Memory Chips. Your Next Laptop Will Pay the Price.
articles.excerpt: DDR5 prices have surged 4-5x, SSDs have doubled, and vendors are restarting DDR4 production lines they thought were retired. Welcome to the RAMpocalypse.
articles.image_caption: Close-up of a DDR memory module on a computer motherboard
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans shopping for laptops — whether for college-bound children, work-from-home setups, or relatives visiting from India — face sticker shock. India's own consumer electronics market and burgeoning gaming industry are also hit. Micron's Gujarat fab, led by Sanjay Mehrotra, is focused on HBM for AI, not consumer DRAM — underscoring the supply trade-off.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wall Street's AI Chip Trade Just Lost $1.3 Trillion in a Single Day
articles.excerpt: Broadcom's cautious guidance and a scorching jobs report combined to trigger the worst semiconductor rout since the pandemic. For NRI investors loaded with chip stocks, the timing is brutal.
articles.image_caption: Stock market trading data on a digital display screen
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans hold massive exposure to semiconductor stocks through direct investment, 401(k)s, and RSU compensation at NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Broadcom, and Micron. The selloff directly hits NRI portfolios and the equity component of H-1B tech workers' total compensation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foxconn Now Makes More Money From AI Servers Than iPhones. Its May Revenue Broke Every Record.
articles.excerpt: The world's largest electronics manufacturer posted a 40 per cent revenue surge on AI rack demand — and India's manufacturing ambitions are next in line.
articles.image_caption: Foxconn founder Terry Gou — the company now earns more from AI servers than iPhones (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Foxconn's India manufacturing expansion could extend to AI server assembly; NRI investors track the Apple-NVIDIA supply chain that Foxconn anchors; India's engineering talent pool positions it for AI infrastructure manufacturing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DeepSeek Just Topped America's Fastest-Growing Software List. The Security Implications Are Enormous.
articles.excerpt: US companies are routing corporate data through Chinese servers to cut AI costs. Indian engineers and IT firms are caught in the crossfire.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang — DeepSeek's rapid enterprise adoption challenges the dominance of American AI providers (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers at OpenAI/Anthropic face revenue pressure as clients explore cheaper Chinese alternatives; Indian IT services firms (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) must navigate data residency risks when clients request DeepSeek integration; Indian AI startups studying DeepSeek's cost-efficient architecture.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AMD Is Shopping Samsung for Its Next Server Chips. TSMC Can't Make Them Fast Enough.
articles.excerpt: Lisa Su's dual-sourcing gambit for 2nm EPYC Venice CPUs could reshape the foundry landscape — and give India's chip ambitions a second suitor.
articles.image_caption: AMD CEO Lisa Su at SXSW 2024
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian engineers at AMD Hyderabad design EPYC processors; Samsung's foundry revival could expand India R&D mandates and give India Semiconductor Mission a second foundry partner beyond TSMC.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Just Brought AI to the World's Cheapest Phones. India Will Feel It First.
articles.excerpt: Gemini Go replaces Google Assistant on Android devices with just 2GB of RAM — a move that could put conversational AI in the hands of 300 million Indians who've never had it.
articles.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google
articles.nri_angle: NRI families have long bought budget Android phones for relatives back home. Those ₹7,000 handsets — the ones that could barely run WhatsApp smoothly — now get the same AI assistant that powers Pixel flagships. For diaspora Indians who've been tech support for their parents' phones, Gemini Go could be the update that finally closes the gap.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Is About to Open an AI Agent App Store. Indian Developers Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: WWDC 2026 kicks off Monday with a revamped Siri, a standalone chatbot app, and what could be the most significant platform shift since the original App Store — an AI agent marketplace.
articles.image_caption: Tim Cook, CEO of Apple Inc.
articles.nri_angle: India is the second-largest source of iOS apps on the App Store. Thousands of Indian developers and startups in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Pune build for Apple's ecosystem. An AI agent marketplace is a new distribution channel — and a new revenue stream — for the same developer community that already supplies a significant share of the enterprise iOS workforce in Silicon Valley.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIT Delhi and Cadence Just Opened a Chip Design Lab. It Could Train India's Missing Semiconductor Workforce.
articles.excerpt: The new innovation lab gives students access to the exact EDA tools used by Intel and TSMC — and offers pre-seed startups a path to first silicon.
articles.image_caption: Cadence Design Systems headquarters in San Jose — the EDA giant has partnered with IIT Delhi to open a chip design training lab (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's semiconductor mission has six approved fabs and a $10 billion government commitment — but the country faces a projected shortage of 75,000 chip design engineers by 2027. For NRI engineers at Cadence, Synopsys, Intel, and Qualcomm, this lab represents the kind of talent pipeline that could eventually supply their teams with India-trained engineers who have worked with the same tools they use daily. For diaspora professionals considering a return to India, the semiconductor sector is becoming a viable career destination — not just in MNC R&D centres but in homegrown startups getting incubation support and a path to tape-out.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Satya Nadella's Microsoft Just Built Its Own AI Brain. OpenAI Should Be Worried.
articles.excerpt: Seven new MAI models, including a trillion-parameter reasoning engine trained from scratch, signal that Microsoft no longer needs its most famous AI partner to compete at the frontier.
articles.image_caption: Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI, who unveiled seven new MAI models at Build 2026
articles.nri_angle: Satya Nadella, the Indian-origin CEO who transformed Microsoft into a $3 trillion company, is now building the AI models that could make OpenAI redundant. For the thousands of Indian engineers at Microsoft — many on H-1B visas — this pivot reshapes their career trajectories. Microsoft AI roles become frontier research positions, not just integration work. And for NRI investors holding MSFT stock, the margin story shifts dramatically when Microsoft runs its own models instead of paying OpenAI per token.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NVIDIA Just Open-Sourced the Biggest AI Model in America. It Runs on a Single Server.
articles.excerpt: Nemotron 3 Ultra packs 550 billion parameters into a hybrid architecture that is five times faster than rivals — and Jensen Huang is giving it away for free.
articles.image_caption: Jensen Huang, NVIDIA CEO, who announced Nemotron 3 Ultra at Computex 2026 in Taipei
articles.nri_angle: NVIDIA employs thousands of Indian engineers across its Santa Clara headquarters, Bangalore R&D centre, and Pune offices. Open-weight models like Nemotron 3 Ultra are particularly significant for India's AI ecosystem: startups like Sarvam AI and Krutrim that cannot afford API costs for proprietary frontier models can now run a competitive alternative on their own infrastructure. For Indian AI researchers and ML engineers at NVIDIA, this release — trained on 20 trillion tokens with open training recipes — represents publishable, career-defining work in the open.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jensen Huang Just Declared War on Apple and Intel. His Weapon Fits in a Laptop.
articles.excerpt: NVIDIA's RTX Spark superchip brings a petaFLOP of AI compute to Windows PCs this fall — and Indian engineers helped build every layer of it.
articles.image_caption: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, who unveiled the RTX Spark superchip at Computex 2026 in Taipei
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers comprise a significant share of NVIDIA's workforce and helped architect RTX Spark. NRI investors holding NVDA stock — up 73% YTD even after Friday's selloff — are watching this diversification into a new $300B+ PC silicon market. Indian AI developers who've relied on cloud GPUs may finally get affordable local AI compute.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AI's Biggest Rivals Just Agreed on One Thing: Their Own Technology Scares Them
articles.excerpt: CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Microsoft signed a joint letter urging Congress to mandate screening of synthetic DNA orders before AI makes bioweapons accessible to amateurs.
articles.image_caption: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, one of the signatories of the biosecurity letter to Congress
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin researchers are deeply embedded in AI safety teams at every signatory company. India's pharmaceutical sector — the world's largest vaccine manufacturer — relies heavily on synthetic DNA for drug development and could face compliance costs from new US screening mandates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Wants Tens of Billions From Shareholders to Build AI. Zuckerberg's Engineers Will Feel It First.
articles.excerpt: Following Alphabet's record $85 billion equity raise, Meta is exploring a massive stock offering to fund up to $145 billion in AI capital expenditure this year — a move that would dilute every employee holding RSUs.
articles.image_caption: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, whose company is exploring a massive equity raise to fund AI spending
articles.nri_angle: Meta employs thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B visas whose compensation is heavily weighted toward RSUs. A large equity offering directly dilutes their net worth. NRI investors holding Meta shares through US brokerage accounts face the same arithmetic.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amazon Built a Warehouse Robot You Can Talk To. It May Replace 160,000 Jobs.
articles.excerpt: The e-commerce giant's next-generation Proteus robot understands conversational language and can operate across entire fulfilment centres — part of a $12 billion European push that previews the automation wave heading for India's logistics sector.
articles.image_caption: An industrial robotic arm — Amazon's new AI-powered Proteus can understand spoken commands to sort and move packages (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Amazon is one of the largest H-1B employers in the US and employs tens of thousands in India. Indian engineers build the AI systems powering these robots, while India's own booming e-commerce sector — with over a million warehouse workers — faces the same automation trajectory.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Wants a Piece of OpenAI. Your AI Stock Options Just Got Complicated.
articles.excerpt: The president is exploring government equity stakes in AI companies, with dividends for every American household. Indian engineers holding RSUs at frontier labs should pay attention.
articles.image_caption: The US Capitol dome in Washington, DC, where AI policy is being reshaped
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian engineers hold RSUs and stock options at AI companies that could be affected. Government equity stakes could dilute holdings, alter IPO valuations, and reshape the wealth-creation engine that H-1B workers have relied on for decades.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic's Mythos Can Find Thousands of Cyber Flaws. The NSA Wants It Anyway.
articles.excerpt: The AI model that got its maker blacklisted by the Pentagon is now being deployed inside America's most secretive spy agency. The Indian engineers caught in the middle are watching closely.
articles.image_caption: The National Security Agency headquarters at Fort Meade, Maryland
articles.nri_angle: Anthropic employs hundreds of Indian-origin AI researchers and engineers. Its CFO Krishna Rao is Indian-origin. The company's ethical stance — refusing to build tools for mass surveillance and autonomous weapons — resonates deeply with Indian American engineers who work across the national security-tech boundary.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sriram Krishnan Is Leaving the White House. He Shaped America's AI Policy on the Way Out.
articles.excerpt: The Chennai-born advisor helped write the playbook for US AI dominance — from Stargate to government equity stakes. Now he's building something new.
articles.image_caption: Sriram Krishnan, Senior White House Policy Advisor on Artificial Intelligence
articles.nri_angle: Krishnan is one of the most powerful Indian Americans in tech policy. His departure raises questions about who will carry the diaspora's voice in AI governance — and whether his planned policy institute will extend Indian-origin influence beyond government.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Just Launched a $14 Billion Consultancy. TCS and Infosys Should Be Nervous.
articles.excerpt: With Forward Deployed Engineers and Palantir-style integration deals, the AI labs are stepping onto the territory Indian IT has owned for three decades.
articles.image_caption: Jernej Furman from Slovenia via wikimedia (BY)
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT services firms (TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant) are the largest H-1B sponsors. If AI labs eat the consulting layer, the model that funds Indian tech immigration is at risk. Every NRI who works at or has family at an Indian IT firm faces a strategic reshaping of their industry.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Private Rocket Company Just Hit $1.1 Billion. Google's Original Backer Lit the Fuse.
articles.excerpt: Skyroot Aerospace, founded by two ex-ISRO scientists, has become India's first space-tech unicorn — backed by Ram Shriram, the same investor who wrote Google's founding cheque.
articles.image_caption: Skyroot's Vikram-S rocket during Mission Prarambh at Sriharikota, India's first private rocket launch
articles.nri_angle: Ram Shriram, one of Silicon Valley's most prominent Indian-American investors (Google's original backer), co-led the round. NRI investors now have a direct proxy for India's private space boom. The deal connects India's deeptech ecosystem to the same capital networks that built Google and SpaceX.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GitHub Copilot Just Killed Flat-Rate AI Coding. Indian Developers Got the Biggest Bill.
articles.excerpt: After June 1, the era of $10-a-month unlimited AI assistance is over. For the world's second-largest developer population, the credit crunch hits different.
articles.image_caption: f09797722911 via flickr (PDM)
articles.nri_angle: India is GitHub's second-largest developer base with 15M+ users. Indian IT services firms (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) deployed 300K+ Copilot seats — now facing surprise cost spikes. Indian startups on tight budgets report 300% increases. H-1B engineers at US companies feel the ripple as teams rethink AI tooling budgets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Is Building Its Own AI Chips. Broadcom's Record Quarter Can't Hide That.
articles.excerpt: Broadcom posted $10.8 billion in AI chip revenue — up 143% — and the stock still cratered. The real story is Google's quiet move toward MediaTek and in-house silicon.
articles.image_caption: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan, who steered the company to record AI chip revenue
articles.nri_angle: Broadcom's Bengaluru R&D centre is one of the company's largest globally. Thousands of Indian engineers design the custom ASICs and networking silicon that powered this record quarter. If Google diversifies away from Broadcom for TPU production, the ripple effects will be felt in cubicles from San Jose to Sarjapur Road.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Agentic AI Has a CPU Problem. It Could Reshape a $120 Billion Market.
articles.excerpt: Everyone bet on GPUs. Now research shows CPUs account for 88% of agentic AI latency. AMD, Intel, Nvidia, and Arm are scrambling for a market that barely existed two years ago.
articles.image_caption: A microprocessor on a motherboard — CPUs are emerging as the hidden bottleneck in agentic AI workloads
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers design CPUs at every company in this race — AMD's EPYC team in Hyderabad, Intel's largest design centre outside the US in Bengaluru, Arm's growing India operation, and Nvidia's Grace CPU team. A $120 billion CPU market shift directly affects career opportunities and specialisation choices for tens of thousands of Indian chip designers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Just Filed for a Trillion-Dollar IPO. Amazon and Google Have Billions Riding on It.
articles.excerpt: The Claude maker's $965 billion valuation and $47 billion revenue run rate set up the largest AI listing ever — with Sundar Pichai's Alphabet and Jeff Bezos's Amazon among the biggest beneficiaries.
articles.image_caption: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, at TechCrunch Disrupt
articles.nri_angle: Amazon and Alphabet, led by Andy Jassy and Sundar Pichai respectively, have invested over $10 billion combined in Anthropic. Indian engineers at both companies hold equity that rises or falls with Anthropic's success. The IPO also intensifies the AI talent war, where Indian-origin researchers are disproportionately represented across frontier AI labs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's UPI Just Went Live in Cambodia. Ten Countries and Counting.
articles.excerpt: NPCI's QR-based payment system now covers 4.5 million Cambodian merchants, part of a methodical push to build a global remittance-killing payments layer.
articles.image_caption: Close-up of a contactless payment using a smartphone and QR code
articles.nri_angle: UPI's international expansion could eventually disrupt the remittance industry that moves $137.7 billion annually to India. For NRIs sending money home through Wise, Western Union, or bank wires, UPI corridors operating at near-zero cost represent a direct alternative. The Cambodia launch is the latest signal that India's payment rails are going global.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Immigrants Built 96 US Unicorns. None Cracked the Top Five.
articles.excerpt: A new NFAP study finds India leads the world in producing billion-dollar startup founders — but the biggest prizes still elude them.
articles.image_caption: Entrepreneur presenting a startup pitch to investors
articles.nri_angle: Indian immigrants have founded 96 US unicorns worth $5 trillion, making India the world's top source of billion-dollar startup founders. IIT Delhi (16 founders) and IIT Bombay (14) are the pipeline. But amid tightening immigration policy and H-1B uncertainty, the infrastructure that enabled this is under threat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS, Infosys, and Wipro Just Deployed AI to 300,000 Workers. Their Stock Crashed Anyway.
articles.excerpt: India's IT giants completed one of the world's largest enterprise AI rollouts in six months. Investors responded by wiping 6% off the Nifty IT index in a single session.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of the Glass Pyramid at the Infosys campus in Mysuru, India
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs have family members working at TCS, Infosys, and Wipro, or hold stock in these companies. The AI disruption paradox — adopt AI or get replaced by it — is deeply personal for the diaspora, especially as Indian IT services firms are the largest H-1B sponsors in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Gave Up on Building Its Own AI Brain. Sundar Pichai and Jensen Huang Won the Contract.
articles.excerpt: The new Siri will run on Google's Gemini models powered by NVIDIA's Blackwell chips — a rare capitulation from the most vertically integrated company on earth.
articles.image_caption: Jensen Huang presenting NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture at CES 2025 in Las Vegas
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin CEOs Sundar Pichai (Google) and Jensen Huang's NVIDIA are the invisible engine behind Apple's biggest AI bet. For the thousands of Indian engineers at all three companies, this partnership reshapes internal power dynamics and career trajectories.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sanjay Mehrotra's Micron Joins the Trillion-Dollar Club. Three Visa Rejections Couldn't Stop Him.
articles.excerpt: The Kanpur-born, BITS Pilani-educated CEO now leads one of America's ten most valuable companies. Three of the world's priciest tech firms are run by Indians who arrived with engineering degrees and middle-class resolve.
articles.image_caption: Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO of Micron Technology, now leads one of America's ten most valuable companies
articles.nri_angle: Mehrotra completes an extraordinary Indian-origin trifecta atop trillion-dollar tech: alongside Satya Nadella at Microsoft and Sundar Pichai at Alphabet. Micron is also building a $2.75 billion ATMP facility in Gujarat — a direct bet on India's semiconductor future.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jensen Huang Called Marvell the 'Next Trillion-Dollar Company.' Its Biggest Lab Is in India.
articles.excerpt: NVIDIA's CEO anointed the networking chipmaker at Computex, sending its stock up 30%. What Wall Street may not know: Marvell's largest R&D centre outside California sits across four Indian cities.
articles.image_caption: Server racks in a modern data center, the kind of infrastructure Marvell's networking chips connect
articles.nri_angle: Marvell employs over 1,000 engineers in Bangalore alone, with additional design centres in Pune, Hyderabad, and Chennai — making it a major employer of Indian semiconductor talent and a key beneficiary of India's chip design ecosystem.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Just Cut the Cybersecurity Team It Paid $5.4 Billion For. AI Got the Budget Instead.
articles.excerpt: Sundar Pichai raised $85 billion last week for AI infrastructure. Days later, Google quietly laid off staff from Mandiant and its Threat Intelligence Group — the elite units that track state-sponsored hackers.
articles.image_caption: Computer code on a dark screen, representing the cybersecurity work now being restructured at Google
articles.nri_angle: Google Cloud employs thousands of Indian engineers, many on H-1B visas. Cybersecurity teams at Google, including Mandiant, have significant Indian representation — and these workers face the 60-day grace period clock if their roles are eliminated.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Tech Workers Built Dallas's Hottest Suburb. Now They're Leaving and Prices Are Cratering.
articles.excerpt: Home prices in Collin County fell 9% as H-1B crackdowns, AI-driven layoffs, and a $100,000 visa fee gut the buyer pipeline that made North Texas boom.
articles.image_caption: Aerial view of a suburban neighbourhood in the United States
articles.nri_angle: Indian H-1B workers drove 70% of luxury home sales in North Dallas suburbs. The collision of 123,000 tech layoffs, a $100,000 H-1B fee, and FHA mortgage bans for non-permanent residents is forcing families to sell at losses or consider returning to India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX IPO Wants $75 Billion From You. Indian Engineers Built Half the Rockets.
articles.excerpt: The largest public offering in history lists next week at a $1.75 trillion valuation. NRI investors face a rare retail window — and an extraordinary price tag.
articles.image_caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 first stage lands at Landing Zone 1 in Cape Canaveral
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers form a significant part of SpaceX's workforce, and NRI investors with Fidelity, Schwab, or Robinhood accounts can participate in the 30% retail allocation — a rare chance to buy into a company that normally only lets insiders in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Cybersecurity Startup Innefu Labs Just Raised $30 Million. Its Client Is the State.
articles.excerpt: The 15-year-old Delhi company builds AI for India's intelligence agencies and defence apparatus. A Singapore-backed Series B now puts it on the path to an IPO.
articles.image_caption: Server infrastructure in a secure data centre facility
articles.nri_angle: Indian defence-tech is emerging as a real career path for NRI engineers at US contractors like Palantir and Raytheon. Innefu's IPO trajectory signals India's growing sovereign AI ambitions and offers NRI investors exposure to a sector that didn't exist five years ago.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nikesh Arora's Palo Alto Networks Just Hit $3 Billion in a Quarter. The Stock Still Fell.
articles.excerpt: The IIT Varanasi grad has turned a firewall company into a $250 billion cybersecurity platform. Wall Street's response to his best quarter yet was to take profits.
articles.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks, at TechCrunch Disrupt
articles.nri_angle: Nikesh Arora's journey from IIT Varanasi to running the world's most valuable cybersecurity company is an instructive arc for Indian-American tech professionals. His platformisation bet mirrors the integration-over-fragmentation instinct that many Indian engineering leaders bring to enterprise tech.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Chip Selloff Just Erased $1 Trillion. Your RSUs Felt Every Dollar.
articles.excerpt: Broadcom's soft AI guidance, a hot jobs report, and rate-hike fears combined to deliver the Nasdaq's worst day in over a year. Indian engineers' stock compensation bore the brunt.
articles.image_caption: Stock market trading screens displaying market data
articles.nri_angle: Indian tech workers in the US hold significant RSU compensation in chip stocks like NVIDIA, AMD, and Micron. A single-day 6-13% decline directly impacts take-home pay, compounding anxiety amid 123,000+ tech layoffs in 2026.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oracle Cut 30,000 Jobs. Twelve Thousand Were in India.
articles.excerpt: The largest single-company layoff in enterprise software history has slashed 40% of Oracle's India workforce — while the company's AI revenue grew 243% and its stock hit record highs.
articles.image_caption: Oracle Corporation headquarters in Redwood City, California
articles.nri_angle: Oracle India was a career anchor for tens of thousands of engineers, DBAs, and ERP specialists who built stable middle-class lives in Bengaluru and Hyderabad. The layoffs have sent shockwaves through a talent pool that feeds the Indian American tech pipeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Satya Nadella Just Publicly Fired at His Own Executive Over an AI 'Addiction' Memo
articles.excerpt: A leaked Microsoft document outlined plans to 'make people addicted' to Scout, the company's new AI agent. Nadella's response was swift, blunt, and sent to 50 top engineers.
articles.image_caption: Satya Nadella, Chairman and CEO of Microsoft
articles.nri_angle: Nadella's rebuke reinforces a Silicon Valley leadership model increasingly shaped by Indian-origin CEOs — one where ethical guardrails on AI are set at the top, not delegated to compliance teams.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
